item.text:
**Bottom line:** `No, not convincingly.` Srettha’s 2024 record has real de-escalation and humanitarian management on the Myanmar border, but the domestic record still shows arbitrary detention of critics, a custodial death, and unresolved impunity for major security-force abuse. I do not see evidence that Thais were clearly safer overall than they were at the start of 2024.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Statement on the Escalation of Conflicts in Myanmar | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-04-18 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand joined ASEAN’s call for immediate cessation of violence, utmost restraint, humanitarian access, and protection of civilians along the Thailand-Myanmar border. This is the strongest direct evidence that Srettha’s government was trying to suppress spillover violence rather than amplify it. | 3B.10; also 3B.7, 3B.9 |
| Positive | Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs visited Mae Sot with a high-level delegation | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-04-23 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/dpmfm-dpmim-dm-nscsg-maesot-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c | A senior civilian-security delegation went to the border to update itself on the situation and support local agencies and people in Mae Sot, with explicit attention to safety and livelihoods. That points to managed crisis response, not militarized spectacle. | 3B.10; also 3B.7, 3B.9 |
| Positive | Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs and ICRC Representatives discuss humanitarian situation in Myanmar | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-04-26 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm-meets-with-icrc-reps-250424-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c | Thailand discussed humanitarian assistance to all groups in need in Myanmar without discrimination. This is relevant to displaced and vulnerable border populations, and it cuts against collective punishment. | 3B.10; also 3B.7, 3B.9 |
| Mixed | Thai PM orders probe into death of activist in pre-trial detention | Reuters via Yahoo News | 2024-05-15 | https://www.yahoo.com/news/thai-pm-orders-probe-death-102023574.html | Srettha ordered an investigation after Netiporn Sanesangkhom died in pre-trial detention. This is a limited accountability response, but it also confirms that the state was still producing serious coercive harm against dissenters. | 3B.10; also 3B.6, 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| Negative | Thailand: New Government Slow to Protect Rights | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/thailand-new-government-slow-protect-rights | HRW said the new government was slow to protect rights and should end politically motivated prosecutions of peaceful protesters and monarchy critics. That suggests the domestic fear climate was still inherited, not resolved. | 3B.10; also 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| Negative | Thai Youth Activist Dies in Custody | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-14 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/14/thai-youth-activist-dies-custody | HRW said Netiporn died in custody after arbitrary arrest and pretrial detention tied to peaceful dissent. This is direct evidence that state coercion still caused avoidable harm rather than making citizens safer. | 3B.10; also 3B.6, 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| Negative | Thailand: Investigate Detained Youth Activist’s Death | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-23 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/23/thailand-investigate-detained-youth-activists-death | HRW noted about 270 activists faced lese-majeste charges and urged a transparent investigation into the custodial death. The article points to selective punishment and continuing insecurity for critics. | 3B.10; also 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| Negative | Thailand: Last-Ditch Effort for Tak Bai Massacre Justice | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-01 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/01/thailand-last-ditch-effort-tak-bai-massacre-justice | HRW said successive Thai governments failed to prosecute officials responsible for deaths and injuries of ethnic Malay Muslim protesters in Tak Bai. That is strong evidence of persistent impunity for communal/security-force violence, undercutting any claim of broad domestic safety gains. | 3B.10; also 3B.7, 3B.9 |

**Assessment**
- The strongest positive evidence is concentrated in the Myanmar-border crisis: restraint, humanitarian access, and coordination with civilian agencies.
- The strongest negative evidence is domestic: prosecutions of critics, custodial death, and long-running impunity for Tak Bai.
- So the best-supported reading is that Srettha reduced some spillover-risk in one regional flashpoint, but did not leave Thai citizens clearly safer overall from domestic political violence and preventable insecurity.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a clean 2024 before/after dataset showing nationwide changes in political violence, communal violence, deaths, injuries, or displacement under Srettha.
- The available evidence is mostly event-based: one de-escalatory border crisis on the positive side, and protest repression / custody abuse / southern-border impunity on the negative side.
- That means the overall safety judgment has to rest on qualitative balance, not on a measurable nationwide trend.
